title: Momotaro the Peach Boy
text:
An old woman was washing clothes in a river when an enormous peach came floating toward her. She carried it home to her husband, and when they cut it open, a baby boy stepped out. The childless couple named him Momotaro, Peach Boy, and raised him. He grew very strong.

When he was grown, Momotaro announced that he would go to Onigashima, the island of the ogres, who had been raiding the land. His mother gave him millet dumplings for the road.

On the way he met a dog, who asked for a dumpling. Momotaro gave him one, and the dog joined him. Then a monkey asked, received a dumpling, and joined. Then a pheasant did the same.

They crossed the sea to the island, where the ogres' fortress had a great gate. The pheasant flew over the walls to scout and then pecked at the ogres' eyes. The monkey climbed the wall and opened the gate from inside. The dog bit at their legs, and Momotaro fought their chief. The ogres were beaten and surrendered, giving up the treasure they had stolen, and Momotaro and his companions brought it home to the old couple.
lesson: Sharing what you have is a good way to build a team. Allies with different abilities, each playing to strength, can take on what none could face alone.
people: Momotaro, a dog, a monkey, a pheasant
date: Japanese folk tradition, recorded from the Edo period
